style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;line-height:normal'><span\nstyle='font-family:Consolas'>           Process log file</span></p>\n\n</span>\n<p><i><b>Note:</b> Some of the files provided as part of the Prime Suite EHI Export will need to be processed through a conversion tool to be unencrypted. The Prime Suite Conversion Tool installation file is available on the My Greenway support portal. Information about exporting and converting single patient or patient population EHI is provided in the Prime Suite online help. </i></p>\n<h2><a name=\"_Root_Export_/\"></a>Root Export / Conversion Folder</h2>\n\n<p>The root folder for the exported / converted files uses the\nfollowing filename format:</p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">SinglePatient_&lt;FileCreatedDateTime&gt; mm-dd-yyyy HH-MM-SS</p>\n\n<p>In the example below, the folder is named SinglePatient,\nfollowed by the date of 08/30/2023 and time of 11:23:27.</p>\n\n<p><img border=0 width=259 height=27 id=\"Picture 5\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image001.jpg\"></p>\n\n<p>Within this root folder will be the following sub-folders:</p>\n\n<p><img border=0 width=297 height=174 id=\"Picture 6\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image002.jpg\"></p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Data_Export_Folder\"></a>Data Export Folder</h2>\n\n<p>The Data Export folder contains the tables of data from the patient’s\nrecords. The folder name will be in this format:</p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">DataExport_SiteID12345_&lt;PatientID&gt;9876</p>\n\n<p>For example, in the image in the root folder, the filename\nis the text Data Export followed by the text Site with a site ID of 350175 and\nthen patient ID of 26955.</p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Table_Files\"></a>Table Files</h2>\n\n<p>In the Data Export folder, each data table is an XML file. The\nfilename format is:</p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">&lt;tablename&gt;.xml</p>\n\n<p>The schema for these XML files is:</p>\n<span style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;Table Name&gt;</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;row&gt; <span\nstyle='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//First record of the table for the\npatient</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:1.0in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;Column 1&gt;Column Value\n&lt;/Column1&gt; <span style='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//first column\nvalue</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:1.0in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;Column 2&gt;Column\nValue &lt;/Column2&gt; <span style='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//second\ncolumn value</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;/row&gt;</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;row&gt; <span\nstyle='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//Second record of the table for the\npatient</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:1.0in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;Column 1&gt;Column\nValue &lt;/Column1&gt; <span style='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//first\ncolumn value</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:1.0in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;Column 2&gt;Column\nValue &lt;/Column2&gt; <span style='font-family:Roboto;color:#70AD47'>//second\ncolumn value</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;/row&gt;</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;line-height:normal'>&lt;/Table Name&gt;</p>\n</span>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n\n<span style=\"display:block; background-color:lightblue; padding:8px;\">\n<h3>How to use the reference information for Data Tables</h3>\n\n<p>The Prime Suite Data Dictionary provides reference\ninformation for each table, including a table description and descriptions of the\nfields in the table. You can open a patient data table and then open the Prime\nSuite Data Dictionary to the table of the same name to perform a side-by-side\nreview of this information.</p>\n\n</span>\n<hr>\n<h2>Document Export Folder</h2>\n\n<p>The Document Export folder contains the documents that were\nexported / converted from the patient’s record in Prime Suite and associated document\ndata. It has this folder name format:</p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">DocumentExport_SiteID12345_&lt;PatientID&gt;9876</p>\n\n<p>The three sub-folders within the Document Export Folder are:</p>\n\n<ul>\n<li>AdamImage contains sketchpad annotations and associated data files</li>\n\n<li>ClinicalBin contains the documents and associated document data files</li>\n\n<li>ImgLibGroupItem contains sketchpad images and associated image data files</li>\n</ul>\n\n<p style='margin-left:.25in;line-height:normal;background:#F8F8F8'><span\nstyle='color:black'><img border=0 width=568 height=157 id=\"Picture 7\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image003.jpg\"></span></p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Document_Drawings_Folder\"></a>Document Drawings Folder (AdamImage)</h2>\n\n<p>This folder is named AdamImage. It contains the sketchpad annotations on drawings. Each\nimage has a folder with the image ID as the name. These images must be reconstructed\nusing the process described in <a href=\"PrimeSuiteEHIExport_Document_Reference.html#ReconstructingAnnotatedDrawings\">Reconstruct Medical Drawings with Patient-Specific Annotations as SVG</a>.</span></p>\n\n<p><img border=0 width=624 height=120 id=\"Picture 12\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image004.jpg\"></p>\n\n<p>Any sketchpad images that in drawings are in the following\nfolder structure:</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;line-height:normal'>AdamImage </p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>Image\nID folder</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>AdamImage_imageID_Data</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>AdamImage_imageID_Document</p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Documents_and_Document\"></a>Documents and Document Data Folder\n(ClinicalBin)</h2>\n\n<p>The Document Export folder is named ClinicalBin. <span\nstyle='line-height:107%;color:#333333'>It contains the documents and document\ndata that was exported from the patient’s medical record in Prime Suite. Each document\nhas a folder with the image ID as the name.</span></p>\n\n<p>Any sketchpad images that in drawings are in the following\nfolder structure:</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;line-height:normal'><span lang=EN>ClinicalBin\n</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'><span\nlang=EN>Document folder</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'><span lang=EN>Document\nData File</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'><span lang=EN>Document File</span></p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Document_Folder\"></a>Document Folder</h2>\n\n<p><span style='line-height:107%;color:#333333'>In the ClinicalBin\nfolder will be a folder for each document with the following name format: </span></p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">&lt;patientID&gt;_&lt;documentID&gt;_&lt;seqID&gt;_&lt;filetypeID&gt;</p>\n\n<p>In the example below, the first document folder has a\npatient ID of ‘26955’, a document ID of ‘5849’, a sequence ID of ‘2’, and a filetype\nID of ‘1005’. </p>\n\n<p><img border=0 width=624 height=158 id=\"Picture 8\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image005.gif\"></p>\n\n<p>Each document folder will contain two files: a data file and\na document file. The file will be in the following format:</p>\n\n<span class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:2px 8px 8px 8px;\">\n\n<p>ClinicalBin_&lt;patientID&gt;_&lt;documentID&gt;_&lt;seqID&gt;_&lt;filetypeID&gt;_Data.xml</p>\n\n<p><span lang=EN>ClinicalBin_&lt;patientID&gt;_&lt;documentID&gt;_&lt;seqID&gt;_&lt;filetypeID&gt;_Document.xml</span></p>\n\n</span>\n\n<p><img border=0 width=624 height=120 id=\"Picture 10\"\nsrc=\"SinglePatientExport_Structure_Schema_files/image004.jpg\"></p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Document_Data_File\"></a>Document Data File</h2>\n\n<p><span style='line-height:107%;color:#333333'>A Document Data\nFile </span>is an XML file located <span style='line-height:107%;color:#333333'>in\na Document Folder. It will have the following filename format:</span></p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\">ClinicalBin_&lt;patientID&gt;_&lt;documentID&gt;_&lt;seqID&gt;_&lt;filetypeID&gt;_Data.xml</p>\n\n<p><span style='line-height:107%;color:#333333'>This file has\nthe document’s details from the Greenway PrimeSuite database table with column\nheadings and document data in the table row. However, it will not have the\ndocument’s raw content.</span></p>\n\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Document_File\"></a>Document File</h2>\n\n<p>Located in a Document Folder, the Document file is the document’s\nraw content in its native file format. It will have the following filename\nformat:</p>\n\n<p class=code style=\"display:block; background-color:lightgray; padding:8px;\"><span lang=EN>ClinicalBin_&lt;patientID&gt;_&lt;documentID&gt;_&lt;seqID&gt;_&lt;filetypeID&gt;_\nDocument.ext</span></p>\n\n<p>where ext is the file extension, which could be any of the supported\nfile formats: PDF, CCDA (xml), TIF, JPG, GIF, BMP, or TXT.</p>\n\n<p>The file may be a document that was created in Prime Suite\nor an externally created document that is stored in Prime Suite. These files\ncan be viewed in applications that support the specific format.</p>\n\n<p>Document file types fall into two categories:</p>\n\n<ul>\n\n<li><b>Generic Document Types.</b> Some documents exported /\nconverted to &nbsp;their original format(s) do not generate any specific\nGreenway proprietary documents that need additional documentation.</span> The\ngeneric document types are listed in the Prime Suite EHI XML Document Reference.</li></br>\n\n<li><b>Greenway Proprietary Document Formats.</b> Some documents generated\nin Prime Suite are in a Greenway proprietary format in XML. Each of these proprietary\nformats is detailed in the Prime Suite EHI XML Document Reference.</li>\n\n</ul>\n<span style=\"display:block; background-color:lightblue; padding:8px;\">\n<h3>How to use the XML Reference for Greenway Documents </h3>\n\n<p>The Prime Suite EHI XML Document Reference provides\nreference information for each document type generated in Prime Suite that has\na Greenway proprietary document format. The reference describes each element in\nthe format. You can open document’s format reference from the data export / conversion\nand then open the table description of the same name in the Prime Suite data dictionary\nto perform side-by-side research of the data.</p>\n</span>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Image_Library_Images\"></a>Image Library Images folder (ImgLibGroupItem)</h2>\n\n<p>This folder is named ImgLibGroupItem<span style='line-height:\n107%;color:#333333'>. It contains the sketchpad drawings. Each image has a\nfolder with the image ID as the name. </span></p>\n\n<p>Any sketchpad images used in a patient document are in the\nfollowing folder structure:</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;line-height:normal'>ImgLibGroupItem </p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-bottom:3.0pt;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>Image\nID folder</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>ImgLibGroupItem_imageID_Data</p>\n\n<p class=code style='margin-top:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-bottom:3.0pt;\nmargin-left:.5in;text-indent:.5in;line-height:normal'>ImgLibGroupItem_imageID_Document</p>\n<hr>\n<h2><a name=\"_Logs_Folder\"></a>Logs Folder</h2>\n\n<p>The Logs folder contains two text files: </p>\n<ul>\n<li>ErrorLog.txt is the log of errors from the export / conversion.</li></br>\n\n<li>ProcessLog.txt is the log of exported / converted files.</li>\n</ul>\n\n</main>\n\n<footer class=\"footer\"></footer>\n\n<!-- Add this button at the end of your body content -->\n<button id=\"scrollTopBtn\" class=\"scrolltop\" For Prime Suite, the documentation consists of five interconnected HTML pages:\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe Prime Suite EHI export produces a **package of XML files** — one file per database table — containing patient data in a simple row-based XML schema:\n\n```xml\n<TableName>\n  <row>\n    <Column1>value</Column1>\n    <Column2>value</Column2>\n  </row>\n  <row>...</row>\n</TableName>\n```\n\nThis is essentially a **database dump in XML format**, with each table from the Prime Suite database exported as a separate XML file. This is a genuine (b)(10) export approach — not a FHIR API repackaged.\n\n### Two Export Modes\n\n1. **Single Patient Export**: Exports all data for one patient. The export package contains:\n   - A `DataExport` folder with one XML file per table\n   - A `DocumentExport` folder with three sub-folders:\n     - `AdamImage` — sketchpad annotations/drawings\n     - `ClinicalBin` — clinical documents in native format (PDF, C-CDA, TIF, JPG, GIF, BMP, TXT)\n     - `ImgLibGroupItem` — sketchpad images\n   - A `Logs` folder with error and process logs\n\n2. **Patient Population Export**: Exports data for all patients at a site.
